yarn-dinkum.meaning: All the advice survives: salt stains, sipping when not thirsty, the ranger snack list ("pretzels, Pringles, chips and cheesy bikkies"), "Sun temperatures are 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter", "not walking between 10am and 4pm", cotton holding water, soaking the hat or bandana.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "keep on top of your water and your tucker", "your sweat dries off quick smart", "if you're not thirsty or peckish", "avoid getting knackered", "knock off late in the arvo", "cotton is ripper", "full of beans". The heading "Stay Watered and Fuelled Up" strains: "watered" is what you do to plants or stock.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Aussie ranger: "it pays to keep on top of your water and your tucker", "chuck in their day packs", "tasty tucker that's ready for the track!". "Stay Watered" is a little forced.
yarn-dinkum.register: A steady level-3 touch through a text that stays practical: "tucker", "quick smart", "bikkies", "peckish", "knackered", "arvo", "ripper"; no swearing, within vulgarity 1.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the friendly, upbeat safety-guide voice: "so don't skip this simple but vital way of cooling down!"
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads cleanly aloud: "Get going before dawn and knock off late in the arvo."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied with little repeated: "tucker", "quick smart", "mightn't", "chuck", "bikkies", "peckish", "knackered", "ripper", "full of beans", "go through the roof".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the park-service hydration and heat guide, same shape and headings: "KEEP YOURSELF DRIPPING WET TO STAY COOL."

engine.meaning: Nearly verbatim, so every point stands: "Sun temperatures are 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter than posted shade temperatures."
engine.sense: The few swaps fit: "Bushwalking in the Grand Canyon", "a late arvo finish", "cotton is ripper in the desert!".
engine.authenticity: What Aussie there is is natural, but US forms remain: "Stay Hydrated and Energized", "stay cool and energized throughout the day", and "bushwalking" sits beside unchanged "hike" ("Experienced desert bushwalkers know that the timing of their hike").
engine.register: Largely untranslated: "To ensure an enjoyable and safe hike, it's important to properly manage hydration and nutrition." Only a handful of swaps ("Bushwalking", "arvo", "ripper", "realise", "favourite"), far below level 3.
engine.tone: The original's chirpy guide tone is intact because the text is: "tasty and trail-ready fuel for the journey!"
engine.flow: Reads as the original does; the swap "you are not bushwalking between the hours of 10am and 4pm" next to "are hiking between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m." is a slight unevenness.
engine.essence: Recognisably the original; it is the original, with nothing retold: "By staying proactive with hydration, nutrition, and rest".

unharnessed.meaning: Complete: "Keep an eye out for salt stains or rings on your clothes", "It's 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter in the sun than the posted shade temperatures", "Get going before sunrise and finish up late arvo", "cotton's great in the desert!".
unharnessed.sense: Every term fits: "you mightn't twig how much fluid you're losing", "keep the tank full", "not running out of puff", "Have a spell somewhere near shade", "staying out of strife", "stay sopping wet".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Aussie: "you've gotta stay on top of your water and your tucker", "It's a simple but bloody effective way to stay cool". The heading "Stay Hydrated and Energized" keeps a US spelling.
unharnessed.register: Level 3 weight, with one mild swear within vulgarity 1: "bloody effective"; "tucker", "twig", "puff", "spell", "strife", "arvo".
unharnessed.tone: Friendly safety guidance, kept: "so don't skip this simple but vital way to cool down!"
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "In the Grand Canyon's hot, dry climate your sweat dries off quick smart, so you mightn't twig how much fluid you're losing."
unharnessed.variety: Wide, unrepeated range: "quick smart", "twig", "chuck", "tucker", "keep the tank full", "running out of puff", "have a spell", "strife", "sopping", "bloody effective".
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the guide: same headings and order, "KEEP YOURSELF SOAKING WET TO STAY COOL."

dinkum-3.meaning: All points are kept: the salt stains, ranger snacks, "It's 15F to 20F (9C-11C) degrees hotter in the sun", "not walking between the hours of 10am and 4pm", soaking clothes and a hat.
dinkum-3.sense: Mostly apt: "a different beast", "hard yakka", "you won't get buggered", "staying out of strife". "the height" for elevation strains (Australians would say altitude), and "a beaut walk" for an enjoyable hike is fine.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds local: "Bushwalking in the Grand Canyon's a different beast", "can be hard yakka, so make sure you're eating enough to keep the engine running", "Tasty tucker, and ready for the track!"
dinkum-3.register: Level 3 weight; "buggered" is within vulgarity 1: "tucker", "cos", "hard yakka", "heaps", "strife", "ripper", "arvo".
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the upbeat advisory voice: "And remember, staying soaking wet isn't just about feeling better."
dinkum-3.flow: Generally smooth, with a couple of clunky joins: "you'll have a heaps better time out on the tracks, and it'll be worth the effort"; "So plan your day so you're not walking".
dinkum-3.variety: Good range, though "tucker" recurs ("your water and your tucker", "Tasty tucker", "water and tucker right", "your tucker and your rest") and "cos" several times.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the guide, same structure and headings: "Stay Hydrated and Keep Your Energy Up".

yarn-troppo.meaning: All the facts survive, with colour added: "terrain that'll give your legs a proper workout", "it's your body waving a little flag at ya", "Don't be one of 'em.". "salt stains or white rings" adds a small detail.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fitting: "keep the tank full", "knackered", "staying out of strife", "full of beans". "It's a crucial bit of kit for hanging on to your energy" strains: kit is gear, and staying wet is not gear.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Leans on stock pastiche: "hot and dry as a dead dingo's donger", "Now listen, cos this one matters.", "eating and drinking like a champ", heavy "ya" ("at ya", "out of ya", "tell ya").
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3: a running yarn voice with asides ("Now here's the catch.", "full stop.", "mate") and a crude simile, "dead dingo's donger", at the edge of vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: The original is a cheerful service guide; this becomes a lecture from a mate: "Now listen, cos this one matters.", "Don't be one of 'em.". Still caring, but the voice shifts more than the brief needs.
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and readable, though the bolted asides interrupt: "That's a common sign you're getting dehydrated, and it's your body waving a little flag at ya."
yarn-troppo.variety: Plenty of terms, but tics repeat: "ya" several times and the engine metaphor twice ("Feed the Engine", "keep the engine running").
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the guide, but the pub-mate framing and new headings ("Keep the Tank Full", "Feed the Engine") push it further from the original's character.

yarn-dinkum.why: "watered" is used of plants and livestock, not people; an odd choice for a heading.

yarn-dinkum.original: To maintain proper hydration, sip water regularly

engine.original: To ensure an enjoyable and safe hike, it's important to properly manage hydration and nutrition.

summaries.yarn-dinkum: Natural, complete and on-brief; one strained term in a heading.
summaries.engine: Barely translated: correct but almost no Aussie, and US spellings left in.
summaries.unharnessed: The best of the set: natural, varied, complete and on-brief; only a US spelling slips through.
summaries.dinkum-3: Idiomatic and complete, a touch repetitive and clunky in places.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Vivid but over-cooked: stock simile and asides push it past level 3 and toward pastiche.
